title: Deterministic Package Fetch Fallback & Controlled Egress SLA for Private Deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood in isolated VPCs or air-gapped environments frequently request a deterministic, operator-driven path for bootstrapping and upgrades that minimizes egress, preserves provenance, and guarantees rollback safety. Current mirror-based approaches are brittle across partial-network conditions and do not provide a clear SLA for allowed egress during operator-driven fetches. Goal: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a controlled egress fallback mechanism and deterministic package fetch protocol that (1) limits external surface area, (2) ensures artifact signature verification and chunked resumable transfer, (3) provides observable SLOs for allowed egress windows during bootstrap and upgrades, and (4) is compatible with operator workflows in disconnected/air-gapped deployments.
scope: In scope: design and acceptance criteria for the deterministic fetch fallback flow, manifest signing and verification rules, minimal egress window SLA and audit logging, operator CLI + Console controls for initiating fallback, and automated health checks post-fetch. Implementation work is out of scope for this ticket but will be represented by ENG follow-ups. This PRD focuses on requirements, constraints, and acceptance tests for private deployments and air-gapped customers.
out_of_scope: Building the full transfer service or mirrors; integrating with every customer KMS provider; end-to-end automation for physical media. Those are follow-up epics. Also out of scope: changing default hosted API behavior for non-private customers.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Deterministic Fetch Flow documented: a step-by-step operator flow (initiate, authenticate, fetch, verify, apply) exists in the PRD and Console runbook.

AC-2: Manifest format and signature: all release artifacts must be referenced by a signed manifest (signed with RH keypair or customer KMS). The manifest schema and verification algorithm are specified and validated by unit tests.

AC-3: Minimal egress window SLA: administrator can configure an egress window (start, duration, allowed hosts) and the platform enforces outbound connections to only those hosts/IPs during the window; policy violations generate alerts and block apply.

AC-4: Chunked resumable transfers: fetch protocol supports resume on partial connections and verifies per-chunk integrity; simulated network interruptions in QA must result in successful resume and final checksum verification.

AC-5: Auditability: every fetch attempt (success/failure), signature verification result, and operator consent event is recorded in the audit log and surfaced in the Console timeline for at least 90 days.

AC-6: Rollback safety: if verification fails at any point, the operator surface prevents partial application and the system rolls back to the previous control-plane-compatible state without requiring additional egress.
AC-7: Observable SLOs: telemetry emits metrics for fetch latency, fetch throughput, manifest validation time, and egress window violations; dashboards and alert thresholds are defined.

AC-8: Compatibility: the flow runs in fully isolated VPCs that only allow outbound connections to customer-defined mirrors or approved proxy endpoints; lab tests validate success in a simulated air-gapped environment using a single outbound proxy host.
AC-9: Security review sign-off: security team approves threat model for temporary egress, KMS usage, and signing key provenance before release gate.
AC-10: Operator UX: Console and CLI include explicit consent modal showing allowed hosts, checksum, and manifest signer fingerprint before starting the fetch; usability review completed.
technical_solution: High-level approach: introduce a deterministic manifest-and-fetch protocol layered on top of existing mirror artifacts. The manifest (JSON) enumerates artifact chunks, checksums, signing keys, and allowed fetch endpoints. An operator-initiated 'egress window' is created with explicit host allowlist and TTL. Fetch clients implement chunked download with resumable offsets and per-chunk HMAC verification. Verification is performed locally against manifest signatures and optionally customer-managed KMS. The control plane enforces temporary iptables/egress ACLs and records audit events. Fallbacks: if mirror fetch fails, operator can optionally enable an ephemeral proxied fetch to a Redwood-signed authoritative host; this flow requires signed consent and a separate audit event.
rollout_plan: Draft PRD + runbook (this ticket) -> 2-week PM review
Security threat-model review and sign-off (security task)
Engineering scoping spike (ENG-19876) -> produce API and CLI contract
Implementation in private-operator beta (canary customers) with observability and audit logs
Usability testing with 3 pilot customers and incorporate feedback
GA gated on security sign-off and passing canary metrics
